chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man buys a slave who has wealth. For whom is his wealth?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If the seller knew that he had wealth, then it is for the buyer, and if he did not know, then it is for the seller.'
ai.seo_question: Who owns a slave's personal wealth when the slave is sold?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal principle of 'ghunm bi al-ghurm' (gain accompanies liability) regarding a slave's personal property (mal) during sale. It establishes that if the seller was aware of the slave's wealth, it transfers to the buyer as part of the transaction; conversely, if the seller was unaware, the wealth remains with the seller, highlighting the importance of disclosure in commercial transactions within Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man buys the owned slave and for him is wealth. For whom is his wealth?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was in the knowledge of the seller that there is wealth for him, so it is for the buyer, and if he did not happen to have knowledge of it, so it is for the seller’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who buys a slave who owns assets; to whom such assets belong?
He (the Imam) said, Tf the seller knows that the slave owns assets then such assets belong to the buyer but if he does not know then they belong to the seller.’”
